Subject: Tertiary processor alignment + EU egress question

Hi David,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we review the DPA for BankingCorp's pilot, our legal and security teams want a precise mapping of the ‘tertiary processors’ you referenced during onboarding — specifically: which third parties may touch telemetry/observability artifacts, where (country) their processing occurs, and whether any of those paths cross non-EEA jurisdictions.

Two concrete asks to unblock our procurement:
- A completed inventory (spreadsheet) listing the tertiary processors, data category (telemetry, logs, metrics), hosting region(s), and whether data is encrypted at rest with customer KMS or Redwood-managed keys.
- An egress/transfer diagram showing any cross-border hops for EU traffic and fallback/onshore routing options.

We appreciate the preliminary list you sent last week but need a version that ties to the DPA exhibits (export paths + legal entity). Can you provide that by EOD Monday (20 May)? Also flag any temporary processors that may be in place during cutover windows and whether we can require temporary onshore-only access for EU customers.

Best,
Lucia

--
Lucia Moreno
Head of Cloud Security Operations
BankingCorp

To: Lucia Moreno <lucia.moreno@bankingcorp.com>

Date: Sat, 18 May 2029 11:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Tertiary processor alignment + EU egress question

Thanks Lucia — appreciate the clarity. Looping in Irene (Privacy), Naomi (Product security), and Kimberly (Partner ops) to confirm details and ownership of the artifacts. I attached a working inventory and a high-level egress map for your review (attached: processor_inventory_v2.xlsx; egress_map_v2029.pdf).

Quick notes based on the current inventory:
- Most telemetry/observability is handled by EdgeSight (primary) and RelayBridge (secondary). Both operate EU-hosted clusters for EU customers; encryption at rest is with Redwood-managed keys by default — we can support customer KMS for Dedicated/Private customers.
- There are two temporary bridges (TransitProxy-A and TempCache-B) used during rolling upgrades; these may briefly cross into a non-EEA control plane during patch windows, but payloads remain encrypted and are not stored persistently outside EU regions.
- Onshore fallback: we offer a routing policy to keep EU traffic within EEA-hosted VMs and fall back to onshore nodes in Germany/France if a regional outage is detected. We can add a contract clause limiting temporary processors for BankingCorp to onshore-only during the pilot.

Action items we can complete by your EOD Monday deadline:
1) Naomi will validate the egress map and call out any transient hops that need stronger contractual language (SOC2 attestation / data residency addendum).
2) Kimberly will populate the legal entity column and provide a DocuSign-friendly exhibit for the DPA (names/addresses for each processor).
3) Irene will prepare a short attestation note describing encryption scope and KMS options for EU accounts.

If anything in the attached inventory looks off, please flag specific rows.

Regards,
David

--
David Kim
Head of Partnerships (EMEA)
